Neha / Jordan — I've drafted a short set of redlines and a recommended Security Exhibit. High-level points and rationale below; full redline attached (proposed-security-exhibit-redlines.docx).

Key proposed language (summary):
1) Audit notice: require Acme to provide 30 days prior notice for any on-site audit. For remote evidence requests, 7 business days notice. This protects customer scheduling and preserves SLOs for customers on shared infra.
2) Scope / staging: pen tests permitted only against a designated staging environment; production access not permitted without a separate written agreement and business justification. All tests must be non-destructive and limited to agreed IP ranges.
3) Evidence types: Redwood will provide SOC 2 Type II report, attestation letters, configuration snapshots, and redacted logs that demonstrate control operation. Redwood will not provide raw customer content or unredacted system logs that could leak customer data.
4) Fix window: Redwood proposes a 10-business-day remediation window for high/critical findings discovered during scheduled pen tests; if a finding is exploitable against production, Redwood will prioritize a hotfix and notify Acme within 24 hours and provide interim mitigations.
5) Confidentiality: any exchange of logs or findings will occur under the Order Form NDA and a separate TLP (Traffic Light Protocol) or mutual NDA clause to protect vulnerability details.

Operational asks for Acme: please confirm whether the 30-day on-site notice and 10-business-day remediation window are acceptable. If you require an accelerated SLA for critical items, we can discuss an SLA addendum in the Order Form.

Attaching redline doc. I left placeholders for exact staging hostnames and contact info.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Contracts

(karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com)
